set.title: Typewright: a calm Mac workspace for TYPO3 content
set.seo_title: Typewright: TYPO3 news, pages, translations and media on your Mac
set.description: Write TYPO3 news, build pages, translate content and manage images in one calm Mac app. Fifteen features, local drafts, TYPO3’s own rules and deliberate publishing.
set.abstract: Typewright is a calm Mac app and web editor for TYPO3: pages and content elements in every language, rich text that keeps TYPO3’s markup, links, media with alt texts, news with local drafts and workspace publishing.

set.header: Write now. Publish when you are ready.
set.subheadline: A calm desktop workspace for TYPO3: write news, build pages, translate content and manage images. Keep drafts on your Mac and send changes to TYPO3 when you decide.

set.header: What does a desktop app add to TYPO3?
set.content:
Writing often happens between meetings, on a train, or with an unstable connection. Typewright keeps the current story and its local draft on your Mac. You can reopen previously loaded articles after an offline restart and continue writing.

Pages work the way TYPO3 shows them: one tree per site, columns from the backend layout and every language of a page side by side. Content elements, links and images follow TYPO3’s own rules, from the element wizard to the link types and the file list.
set.sidebar_content:
TYPO3 remains in charge

Your backend user, permissions and workspace rules still apply. A local draft is not a server save. Nothing uploads or publishes in the background.

The backend remains the place for extension settings, user management, complete page configuration and collection entries that need adding or sorting.

set.header: Less friction between an idea and an article
set.subheadline: Features that improve the writing workflow without taking publishing away from TYPO3.

match.title: Local drafts, separate from the server

set.title: Local drafts, separate from the server
set.description: After a short pause, the app saves your writing locally. Drafts are kept separately for each website, user, workspace and article.

set.title: Continue through interruptions
set.description: Previously loaded articles and their local drafts remain available after an offline restart. New articles from the server and uploads wait for a connection.

set.title: A native Mac workflow
set.description: Use ⌘S to send changes to TYPO3, ⌘N to begin a news article and ⌘K to search. Native menus, zoom and save notifications fit the way you work.

set.title: Encrypted sessions
set.description: The Mac app encrypts session tokens with Electron safeStorage. Passwords are never saved. The web editor keeps tokens in the current browser session.

set.title: Clear workspace review
set.description: Save in a TYPO3 workspace, review the staged changes and explicitly approve publishing. Server permissions and policy refusals are respected.

set.title: One interface, several websites
set.description: Remember website addresses and usernames, then sign in to the site you need. The same interface also runs in the browser.

set.header: From the first connection to a published page
set.content:
1. Connect: enter the HTTPS address of your TYPO3 installation and sign in with your backend administrator account. The Typewright connector must be installed; news editing requires EXT:news.
  2. Write and build: pick an article or a page. Add elements from TYPO3’s element wizard, link pages and files, and add images with alt texts.
  3. Translate: switch the language tab, translate missing elements with one click and compare with the original under each field.
  4. Send: choose a workspace before editing when you want a review step. Saving sends the content to that workspace. Publishing requires a separate confirmation.
set.sidebar_content:
Current beta

This beta requires an active backend administrator account; scoped editor roles are not supported yet. The tested desktop build is for macOS on Apple Silicon. It is unsigned and not notarized. The browser version is built from the same source.

The connector is installed from the private GitLab repository. Ask us for access or a guided demonstration.

match.title: Can I replace the TYPO3 backend with this?

set.title: Can I replace the TYPO3 backend with this?
set.content: Not completely. Typewright covers everyday editing: news, pages, content elements, translations, links and images. Use the backend for extension settings, user management, complete page configuration and collection entries that need adding or sorting.

set.title: Which languages can I edit?
set.content: Every language of the site. Each page shows a tab per language with the number of translated elements. Translating uses TYPO3’s own command, so translations stay connected to the original, and the original text is shown under each field.

match.title: Does it follow TYPO3’s rules for links and files?

set.title: Does it follow TYPO3’s rules for links and files?
set.content: Yes. Links are stored the way TYPO3 stores them (t3:// links for pages, files, folders and records), so the website and the backend link browser understand them. Images stay in TYPO3’s file list; alt texts and other texts for one use are file references with the file’s metadata as fallback.

match.title: How does a new page start?

set.title: How does a new page start?
set.content: Hidden. The page assistant creates it at the position you choose, with its URL path, the translations you want and a first element. You publish it when it is ready.

match.title: What happens when the connection drops?

set.title: What happens when the connection drops?
set.content: You can continue editing an already loaded article. Local drafts and cached articles survive a restart. Sending changes to TYPO3 and loading new server content require a connection.

match.title: Is a local draft already visible on the website?

set.title: Is a local draft already visible on the website?
set.content: No. Local drafts remain on the device. Saving sends them to TYPO3. In a draft workspace, a separate explicit publication step is required before those changes go live.

match.title: Does it bypass permissions or publish automatically?

set.title: Does it bypass permissions or publish automatically?
set.content: No. The connector executes under the backend user’s permissions and the abilities policy. Publishing only sends approval after you confirm the publication dialog.

set.title: Who provides the app?
set.content: Typewright is an independent webconsulting application for TYPO3. It is not an official product of TYPO3 GmbH or the TYPO3 Association.

match.title: What happens to markup the editor cannot show?

set.title: What happens to markup the editor cannot show?
set.content: It stays. Abbreviations, sub- and superscript, language spans and classes are kept while you edit. A field with markup the visual editor cannot represent opens as HTML with a note, and switching to the visual editor asks first.

match.title: Can I publish a workspace from the app?

set.title: Can I publish a workspace from the app?
set.content: Yes, after you confirm. The review lists every change in the workspace, new records included. Publishing uses TYPO3’s own workspace commands and reports what was published and what TYPO3 refused.

set.header: Try a calmer way to edit TYPO3
set.content: Bring one of your editorial workflows: a news article, a page in two languages, a set of images. We will show where the Mac app saves time and which tasks should stay in your backend.

set.header: Typewright: a calm Mac workspace for TYPO3 content
set.content: Write news, build pages, translate content and manage images in one calm Mac app. Fifteen features, local drafts; TYPO3 controls permissions and publishing.
